items.title: Reduce service account token exposure
items.rationale: Mounted service account tokens expand blast radius when a pod is compromised and should be disabled unless the workload truly needs Kubernetes API access.
actions: Set automountServiceAccountToken: false for workloads that do not need the API.
Use a dedicated least-privilege service account when API access is required.
Keep token mounts read-only and review RBAC bindings.

items.title: Mount the root filesystem read-only
items.rationale: Writable root filesystems make persistence and tampering easier after compromise.
actions: Move writable paths to explicit emptyDir or persistent volumes.
Validate startup scripts and temp directories still work after the change.
items.snippet:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: REPLACE_ME
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: target-gvisor,role=target
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      containers:
      - name: REPLACE_ME
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          runAsGroup: 10001
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
          seccompProfile:
            type: RuntimeDefault

kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: sandbox-restricted
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Audit
  rules:
  - name: require-restricted-security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: Enforce restricted securityContext for sandbox workloads.
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - securityContext:
              allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
              readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
              seccompProfile:
                type: RuntimeDefault
templates.gatekeeper_template:
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8srequiredsandboxsecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sRequiredSandboxSecurity
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8srequiredsandboxsecurity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem
        msg := "Sandbox pods must set readOnlyRootFilesystem=true"
      }

ai_advisor.executive_summary: Two high-severity issues detected for Deployment sandbox-gvisor/target-gvisor: a service account token is automounted into pods (SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN) and the container root filesystem is writable (ROOTFS_RW). Both increase risk if the pod is compromised. fixes are not auto-applied due to potential workload breakage.
ai_advisor.remediation_overview: Validate whether the workload needs in-cluster API access and which paths must remain writable. Then either disable automounting of the service account token and/or set readOnlyRootFilesystem after moving writable paths to explicit volumes (emptyDir) or other writable mounts. Apply changes with operator approval and test.

prioritized_groups.title: Credentials exposure
prioritized_groups.rationale: Automounted tokens allow privilege escalation and lateral movement; high severity and broad blast radius.

prioritized_groups.title: Filesystem integrity
prioritized_groups.rationale: Writable root filesystem enables persistence and tampering if container is compromised; requires compatibility checks.

item_advice.explanation: Pods currently have the service account token automounted, exposing cluster credentials to any process in the container.
item_advice.operator_impact: Disabling automount will break any in-pod code that calls the Kubernetes API (e.g., controllers, mutating agents).
item_advice.validation_advice: Search pod/container logs and code for Kubernetes client usage; test in dev by creating a copy of the Deployment with automountServiceAccountToken: false and run API-dependent flows.
item_advice.ordering_reason: Reduce credential exposure first to limit immediate attack surface.

item_advice.explanation: Containers run with a writable root filesystem, allowing an attacker to modify binaries/config or persist files.
item_advice.operator_impact: Enabling readOnlyRootFilesystem may break the app if it writes to /tmp, /var, /etc, or application directories; requires explicit writable volumes for those paths.
item_advice.validation_advice: Identify runtime writable paths (lsof, strace, or instrumented run); create emptyDir or PVC mounts for needed write locations and test a Deployment copy with securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true.
item_advice.ordering_reason: After confirming writable paths and adding volumes, enable read-only root to harden filesystem.

ai_advisor.guided_operator_message: Confirm whether this workload needs Kubernetes API access and identify writable paths; then apply token automount disabling and readOnlyRootFilesystem in a tested Deployment copy before rolling to production.
warnings: Do not disable automountServiceAccountToken if the pod or sidecars call the Kubernetes API.
Do not enable readOnlyRootFilesystem until all required writable paths are mounted explicitly.
Workload runs on runtimeClass gvisor; validate compatibility after changes.
next_steps: Search code and containers for Kubernetes client usage and decide if API access is required.
Create a non-production Deployment copy and set automountServiceAccountToken: false to test API-related functionality.
Identify writable filesystem paths and add explicit emptyDir/PVC mounts for them.
Test setting securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true in the test Deployment.
After successful tests, roll changes to production with monitoring and rollback plan.
